I had a connecting flight a few months ago, and on paper it looked totally fine.
Same airport, ninety minutes between flights, nothing to worry about.
I landed, grabbed my bag, and just started walking toward my next gate, feeling pretty relaxed about the whole thing.
I checked the screen, saw the gate number, and figured I basically knew where I was going.
I mean, I'd flown through that airport before, so I wasn't exactly nervous.
I just walked in a straight line, past the shops, past a coffee place I sort of wanted to stop at, and kept going.
About ten minutes in, I noticed the gate numbers weren't lining up the way I expected.
They kept jumping around, skipping ranges, nothing like a normal sequence.
I stopped, looked at the board again, and realized my gate wasn't even in this terminal.
It was in a completely different one, connected by a shuttle train I hadn't planned on taking at all.
I found the train, and of course, it was one of those slow ones that stops at every single station along the way.
I stood there watching the doors open and close, open and close, checking the time every few seconds like that would somehow make it move faster.
I got off, and I still had a fair walk ahead of me.
So I started half-jogging, dragging my bag behind me, dodging a cart, apologizing to a guy I nearly ran into near a bookstore.
My shirt was sticking to my back by the time I saw the gate number on a sign.
I got there just as they were closing the doors, and the agent looked at my ticket, sort of winced, and told me the flight was already boarded and locked.
I explained the whole terminal thing, a little out of breath, hoping that might change something, but honestly, it didn't.
She was pretty kind about it, though.
She pulled up the next available flight, which wasn't until the next morning, and used some travel voucher to book me a room at the airport hotel for the night.
I guess that's one small upside of connecting flights going wrong, they usually know exactly how to handle it.
I spent that evening eating a sad airport dinner, texting a friend about my terrible luck, and watching planes take off from a window near my gate.
It wasn't exactly the evening I'd planned, but I got a decent night of sleep, and honestly, that hotel bed felt amazing after all that running.
The next morning, I got up early, checked the terminal about four times before even leaving my room, and made it to my new flight with time to spare.
Now, whenever I book a connection, I actually check which terminal each flight uses, instead of just assuming everything's in one place like I did that day.
